newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Senate slightly amends broadcasting bill.
newsitem.headline: French Senate slightly amends broadcasting bill.

text.p: The French Senate slightly changed a bill that will redefine certain aspects of broadcasting in France, accepting an opposition amendment stipulating that 20 percent of radio frequencies for independent operators be reserved for French-language broadcasting.
But it rejected an opposition call seeking to ban contracts giving television channels exclusive rights to broadcast public TV channels by satellite.
The Senate's changes are due to be examined by the National Assembly, the lower house of Parliament, by mid-March.

The Senate, the upper house of Parliament, approved the centre-right government's proposals on radio and an amendment lengthening the mandate of chairmen of public channels to five years from three currently.
The government's proposals aim to make more flexible the procedure candidates must follow for the attribution of radio frequencies.

They also cover the renewal of authorisation of radio frequencies and make local advertising a criterion for the CSA, the French broadcasting regulator, to take into account in attributing frequencies.
The Senate approved recommendations imposing quotas for French and European programmes broadcast from abroad.
It also created a working group of Parliamentarians and broadcasting representatives to look at advertising used during the broadcast of regional programmes on terrestrial channels.
An amendment allowing the possibility of broadcasting national advertising during regional programmes on private channel M6 was withdrawn.
